translationRepairs: In 962, Dou Yi, Minister of Works, was appointed to preside over the court.
In 961, Dou Yi, Minister of Works, was appointed to preside over the court.
建隆二年 is Jianlong 2; Jianlong 1 = AD 960, so the year is AD 961, not 962 (outside-knowledge conversion).

In 1089, at the Ministry of Justice's request, the court's rules were revised: officials who misjudged five or more penal-servitude cases, or two capital cases, were exempt from selection restrictions.
In 1089, at the Ministry of Justice's request, the court's rules were revised: officials who misjudged five or more penal-servitude cases, or two capital cases, were barred from selection.

不在選限 means such officials were excluded from selection, not exempted from its restrictions; the English reverses the rule (the note in s0046 shows the threshold was being relaxed from three/one to five/two).

For the Zhou, Song, and Yi imperial tomb temples, commissioned officials made seasonal offerings. For mourning ceremonies, imperial clansmen and officials were classified by mourning garment and rank, and rules for imperial condolence visits and funeral gifts were proclaimed.

For the temples of the Later Zhou imperial tombs Song, Qing, and Yi, commissioned officials made seasonal offerings. For mourning ceremonies, imperial clansmen and officials were classified by mourning garment and rank, and rules for imperial condolence visits and funeral gifts were proclaimed.
周嵩、慶、懿陵 lists three Zhou imperial tombs (嵩陵, 慶陵, 懿陵); the English drops 慶 (Qing) and makes "Zhou" look like a separate tomb.

In May 1070, an edict ordered the Regulatory Office to balance the empire's finances. The Ever-Normal policy was assigned to the Court of the National Granaries, which gained additional assistants and registrars and took charge of implementing the farmland, waterworks, corvée exemption, and baojia laws.

In the fifth month of 1070, an edict ordered the Regulatory Office to balance the empire's finances. The Ever-Normal policy was assigned to the Court of the National Granaries, which gained additional assistants and registrars and took charge of implementing the farmland, waterworks, corvée exemption, and baojia laws.
五月 is the fifth lunar month; rendering it as Gregorian "May" invents a Western month.
For tribute goods, they were presented on imperial order, and after memorial review approval in daylight, disbursement was permitted.
For tribute goods, they were presented on imperial order, and after the memorial was reviewed and received the imperial endorsement, disbursement was permitted.
得晝 here means obtaining the imperial endorsement (晝/畫, the emperor marking a document); "in daylight" is a mistranslation.

(Emperor Shenzong often resented Khitan intransigence and burned with the ambition to recover You and Yan. He amassed gold and silk in the inner treasury and composed a four-line poem: "The Five Dynasties lost the realm; the northern foe ran rampant.

(Emperor Shenzong often resented Khitan intransigence and burned with the ambition to recover You and Yan. He amassed gold and silk in the inner treasury and composed a poem in four-character verse: "The Five Dynasties lost the realm; the northern foe ran rampant.
四言詩一章 is a stanza of four-character verse; the poem quoted runs to eight four-character lines, so "four-line poem" is wrong.
In 1127 an edict abolished the Court of the Imperial Treasury and transferred its functions to the Gold Bureau.
During the Jianyan era (1127-1130) an edict abolished the Court of the Imperial Treasury and transferred its functions to the Gold Bureau.
建炎 names only the reign period, not its first year; "In 1127" invents a precise year (outside-knowledge span of Jianyan: 1127-1130).

The court also ordered Supervising Secretary Sun Jue, Vice Director of the Secretariat Gu Lin, Chongzheng Hall Lecturer Cheng Yi, and the Imperial Academy's chief and vice directors to review and draft new academy regulations.

The court also ordered Supervising Secretary Sun Jue, Vice Director of the Palace Library Gu Lin, Chongzheng Hall Lecturer Cheng Yi, and the Imperial Academy's chief and vice directors to review and draft new academy regulations.
秘書少監 is the vice director of the Palace Library (秘書省), not of the Secretariat (中書省).
The court also established one doctor of the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》; in 1089 one additional Vice-Director was added.
The court also established one doctor of the 《Spring and Autumn Annals》; in 1087 one additional Vice-Director was added.
二年 continues the Yuanyou 1 (AD 1086) sequence, so it is Yuanyou 2 = AD 1087, not 1089 (outside-knowledge conversion).

Zhai Si of the Left Remonstrance Bureau said: "The Yuanfeng 《Imperial College Statutes》 already provide full rules for instruction and discipline; now that New Text classicism has been restored for recruitment, he asked the responsible offices to review and reissue them."

Zhai Si of the Left Remonstrance Bureau said: "The Yuanfeng 《Imperial College Statutes》 already provide full rules for instruction and discipline; now that selection of officials by essays on the meaning of the classics has been restored, I ask that the responsible offices review them and reissue them as before."
追復經義取士 means restoring recruitment by classical-exegesis essays, not "New Text classicism"; the quotation also slips into third person ("he asked") though 乞 is the speaker's own request.

In 1126 Remonstrance and Policy Grandee Feng Xi said: "The court has lifted the Yuanyou ban on rival scholarly schools and no longer enforces Wang Anshi's learning alone; whichever interpretation of the 《Six Classics》 is sound should be accepted; yet some schools still cling to partisan doctrines; he asked that responsible offices investigate, and that officials who let private bias govern teaching be severely punished."

In 1126 Remonstrance and Policy Grandee Feng Xi said: "The court has lifted the ban on Yuanyou scholarship and no longer enforces Wang Anshi's learning alone; whichever interpretation of the 《Six Classics》 is sound should be accepted; yet some schools still cling to partisan doctrines; I ask for an edict ordering the responsible offices to examine them, and that those who dare let private likes and dislikes govern selection be severely dismissed and punished."

元祐學術之禁 is the ban on Yuanyou scholarship (the learning of the Yuanyou partisans), not a ban issued in Yuanyou on "rival schools"; the quoted request (願詔有司考校) is in the speaker's own voice and concerns selection (去取), not teaching.
In 1134 two instructors for the great and small schools of the princely palaces were restored; in 1163 one post was cut.
In 1134 two instructors for the great and small schools of the princely palaces were restored; in the Longxing era one post was cut.
隆興 names only the reign period (1163-1164); "in 1163" invents a precise year.

In December 1216 the Clan Academy was restored; instructors became doctors, and a Clan Academy instructor was added. All posts were placed under the Court of Imperial Clan Affairs, below Court of Imperial Sacrifices doctors but with the instructor above Imperial Academy rectifiers. Salaries and honors followed Imperial Academy doctor and rectifier precedents, and distant clansmen were at last able to enroll.

In the twelfth month of 1216 the Clan Academy was restored; instructors became doctors, and a Clan Academy instructor was added. All posts were placed under the Court of Imperial Clan Affairs, below Court of Imperial Sacrifices doctors but with the instructor above Imperial Academy rectifiers. Salaries and honors followed Imperial Academy doctor and rectifier precedents, and distant clansmen were at last able to enroll.
十二月 is the twelfth lunar month of Jiading 9 (written 喜定 in the text), not Gregorian December.

【Library Official】 In 994 Imperial Academy chief commissioner Li Zhi said: "The Imperial Academy long maintained an office for book printing, funds, and supplies under a rather inelegant name; I ask that it be renamed the Imperial Academy library official."
李誌言 is "Li Zhi said"; 言 is the verb, not part of the name (the same official appears as 李至 in s0256).
【Directorate of Imperial Construction】 Under the old system there was one chief commissioner, filled by a court official of sixth rank or higher.
【Directorate of Imperial Construction】 Under the old system there was one chief commissioner, filled by a court official or higher.
以朝官以上充 says only "court officials and above"; "sixth rank" is not in the source.

Policy for builders and craftsmen and capital repairs belonged to the Three Departments' Construction Section; the directorate itself only supplied provincial sacrificial-animal plaques, anchor stones, incense, hand-washing vessels, and tablet-offerings and silks for sacrifices.

Policy for builders and craftsmen and capital repairs belonged to the Construction Section of the Three Offices (Finance Commission); the directorate itself only supplied provincial sacrificial-animal plaques, anchor stones, incense, hand-washing vessels, and tablet-offerings and silks for sacrifices.
三司修造案 is a section of the Three Offices (三司, the finance commission), not the Three Departments (三省); cf. s0042.

【Directorate for Arms】 Early in the dynasty military equipment was handled by the Armor Section of the Three Offices (Finance Commission), with no dedicated office.
三司胄案 is a section of the Three Offices (三司, the finance commission), not the Three Departments (三省).

The directorate also coordinated prefectures and capital workshops in divided production and used comparisons to promote or dismiss its officials. One assistant was cut in 1088 and restored during the Shaosheng era.
元祐三年 is Yuanyou 3 = AD 1088, not 1098 (outside-knowledge conversion).

Early in 1174, an edict forbade removing weapons from the depot except when they were being presented to the throne, and presentation and inspection were gradually reduced.
非進入 means "unless being sent in (to the palace)"; nothing in the source concerns tribute.

From then on, directors and vice-directors were allowed to oversee supply while holding other posts, though both men had initially held concurrent Ministry of Revenue duties.
版曹 is the Ministry of Revenue (戶部, keeper of household registers), not a Board of Works.

An office was established at Chanzhou, called the Outer Directorate.
澶州 is read Chanzhou, not Dazhou.

and in a third year (the reign period is not named; presumably Chongning 3, 1104) the post was restored.

In 1118 Minister of Works Wang Zhao requested that experienced former water officials be appointed as the southern and northern outer assistants; the request was approved.

Under the Yuanfeng reforms, the Directorate of Astronomy was abolished and the Grand Astrologer Bureau was established under the Palace Library.
